records.name: Sao Paulo
records.summary: Mixed picture: Sao Paulo led the national ranking in 2024 with 16 killings of travestis and trans people, then fell to 4 recorded killings in 2025 - out of the top group. The country's dominant geographic pattern applies here: at least 68% of the 2024 killings (83 of 122) happened outside state capitals, in interior cities, so the risk sits in Sao Paulo's interior rather than the capital.

records.name: Puducherry
records.summary:
Puducherry is a union territory with a partial legislature: recognition and welfare policy for trans people is set principally by the federal government, and no Puducherry-specific statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is on file.

The framework that governs it shifted sharply in March 2026: parliament passed an amendment removing the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricting legal recognition to historically recognised communities (hijra/kinnar) and intersex people, mandating medical certification for identity documents and for surgery; critics and a court-appointed advisory panel warn it excludes many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people, protests followed the vote in several cities, and the change bears uniformly on every state and territory.

Nationally recurring policing practice — treating trans appearance as a suspicion category in transit spaces, evidenced by an August 2024 railway-platform groping complaint (an FIR was filed and intrusive questioning reported) — reaches union-territory visitors through federal transport policing rather than any local law.

records.name: Lakshadweep
records.summary:
No Lakshadweep-specific trans statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is on file. As a union territory without a full legislature, its recognition policy is set by the central government.

That national framework narrowed sharply in March 2026: parliament passed an amendment removing the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricting legal recognition to historically recognised communities and intersex people, and requiring medical certification — critics warn many trans and non-binary people will be excluded, a court-appointed advisory panel asked for withdrawal, protests followed the vote, and presidential assent is pending. Whatever the island's local society, the recognition machinery facing a visitor or resident runs through that national law.
